_readFirst: Facts below are machine-checkable against the sibling raw-part files and the two .xlsx fixtures in this directory. Prose citations/caveats are in README.md and the research report delivered alongside this fixture set. Compare against ../xlsx-note-reference/manifest.json for the legacy-Notes-only baseline.

contentTypes.source: learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-xlsx/66e1875d-... (Threaded Comments part) and .../1a170d26-... (Persons part); confirmed byte-for-byte in docling-content-types.xml and elden-content-types-excerpt.xml

partPaths.numberingScheme: CORRECTED 2026-09-27 (design review 1, F2) -- the original text here, based on inspecting only 2 of elden's 9 commented sheets, wrongly claimed 'only sheets 1 and 5 have comments'. Re-verified directly against every sheet's own worksheet.xml.rels: elden has 10 sheets, and 9 of them carry comments (only sheet 4, 'Sorceries & Incantations List', has none). N runs 1 through 9 in the SEQUENTIAL ORDER of sheets that have any comment, skipping the one uncommented sheet's number entirely rather than reserving it: sheet1->N=1, sheet2->N=2, sheet3->N=3, sheet4->(no parts), sheet5->N=4, sheet6->N=5, sheet7->N=6, sheet8->N=7, sheet9->N=8, sheet10->N=9. N is shared between comments{N}.xml and threadedComment{N}.xml for a given worksheet, but is NOT tied to that worksheet's own position/sheetId -- docling's single-sheet file (N=1) is consistent with this but too small to show the gap-skipping behavior on its own.
partPaths.personsPartIsSingular: Exactly one xl/persons/person.xml per workbook (not per worksheet), shared by every threadedComment part via personId. Confirmed in both fixtures.

relationships.implicitMeansNoRidInContent: MS-XLSX calls both the threadedComment and person relationships 'implicit' (ISO/IEC29500-1 12.3.24 / 12.3.23): the Relationship entry IS present in the .rels part, but NO r:id attribute anywhere in the worksheet/workbook XML content points at it -- Excel finds these two parts purely by relationship Type. Contrast with vmlDrawing, which the worksheet DOES reference explicitly via <legacyDrawing r:id="..."/>, and with the legacy comments relationship, which is likewise never referenced by r:id in worksheet content. Confirmed by diffing sheet1.xml content against sheet1.xml.rels in both fixtures: only legacyDrawing's rId appears in the worksheet body.

guidFormat.specPatternSource: ECMA-376 ST_Guid simple type: xsd:pattern value="\{[0-9A-F]{8}-[0-9A-F]{4}-[0-9A-F]{4}-[0-9A-F]{4}-[0-9A-F]{12}\}" -- strictly UPPERCASE hex per the schema (via randym/axlsx mirror of the ECMA-376 shared-commonSimpleTypes.xsd; MIT-licensed mirror, not the primary ECMA/ISO document itself)
guidFormat.realWorldCaseVaries: Windows Excel and Mac Excel samples write UPPERCASE hex (docling fixture: {ED88F4F5-A552-4A41-970D-6B23DC2319F4}). Google Sheets export writes LOWERCASE hex (elden fixture: {7d3fab4d-4ec3-48eb-ae3d-c29f489f62a2}), which is technically non-conformant to the strict XSD pattern above but is accepted by Excel on read. A writer should emit uppercase to match the spec and the majority of real Excel output; a reader must match case-insensitively.

timestampFormat.pattern: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ff (exactly 2 fractional-second digits, no timezone offset, no trailing Z)
timestampFormat.note: Every dT value across both fixtures (dozens of samples) uses this exact 2-decimal, no-Z shape. XSD type is xsd:dateTime (which permits a Z/offset), so a writer COULD add one and stay schema-valid, but no real sample seen writes one. Treat local-naive 2-decimal as the de facto format; do not assume UTC.

threadedCommentAttributes.root: First message of a thread: has personId + id (both required GUIDs), ref (optional per XSD but always present in real samples), dT, optional done ("1"=resolved; real Excel samples OMIT done entirely when false, real Google Sheets samples write done="0" explicitly when false), text child element. Never has parentId.
threadedCommentAttributes.reply: Has parentId set to the ROOT's id -- confirmed with a 3-reply thread and a 4-reply/5-root/9-message-total cell (B19; see multipleThreadsPerCell below -- CORRECTED 2026-09-27, design review 1 F2: previously miscounted as '8-reply/9-message', which is arithmetically inconsistent with itself; recounted directly from elden-threadedComment1-B19-excerpt.xml's 9 ref="B19" elements: 5 have no parentId (the roots), 4 have one) that ALL replies point at the same root id, never chained reply-to-reply, even when replies span many days from different authors. done never observed on a reply element.
threadedCommentAttributes.textElement: <text> (default-ns) or <x18tc:text> (prefixed) child element holds the plain-text comment body; xml:space="preserve" is written explicitly by Google Sheets, omitted by Excel (both preserve whitespace correctly regardless since XML default is to preserve unless told otherwise by the consuming app's own trimming).

multipleThreadsPerCell.finding: A single cell ref (e.g. "B19") can carry SEVERAL INDEPENDENT top-level threadedComment roots, not just one thread with nested replies. Confirmed directly: elden-threadedComment1-B19-excerpt.xml has 5 separate root ids all with ref="B19" (some with their own replies, some without), spanning dT from 2022-04-27 to 2023-01-22 -- i.e. a resolved thread does not get reopened by a later comment on the same cell; a new 'New Comment' action starts a brand-new root. elden-comments1-B19-excerpt.xml correspondingly has 5 separate <comment ref="B19"> legacy placeholder blocks, one per root, each with its own tc={id} author.
multipleThreadsPerCell.implication: A reader/writer MUST group threadedComment elements by (ref, id-chain), never assume a single ref implies a single thread, and must be prepared to emit/parse multiple legacy <comment> placeholders sharing one ref.

personAttributes.schema: displayName (required, string), id (required, GUID, matches threadedComment personId), userId (optional, string), providerId (optional, string)

providerId: None (Mac Excel, local/non-AAD account -- docling fixture)
google-sheets (every person in the elden fixture)
Windows Live (reported in a third-party GitHub issue, not in our saved fixtures -- see README)
realValuesSeen.userId: Mac/Windows Excel local accounts repeat the displayName string itself as userId (odd but confirmed in docling: userId="Jane Smith (JS)" for displayName="Jane Smith (JS)"). Google Sheets OMITS userId entirely on every person entry in the elden fixture (57 entries checked, none have userId).

legacyPlaceholder.sharedSentence: [Threaded comment]\n...Your version of Excel allows you to read this threaded comment; however, any edits to it will get removed if the file is opened in a newer version of Excel. Learn more: https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=870924
legacyPlaceholder.urlConfirmedAcross3IndependentSources: docling fixture (Mac Excel), elden fixture (Google Sheets export), and PHPOffice/PhpSpreadsheet issue #2184 (independent real-Excel-365 sample quoted in that issue) -- all three use the identical fwlink URL and near-identical sentence.

whitespaceLayoutVaries.excelVariant: blank line after '[Threaded comment]', blank line before 'Comment:', 4-space indent under 'Comment:'/'Reply:' lines, one 'Reply:' block per reply, no trailing newline seen -- see docling-comments1.xml
whitespaceLayoutVaries.googleSheetsVariant: single space (not blank line) before 'Your version...', no blank line before 'Comment:', TAB indent (not 4 spaces), trailing newline, xml:space="preserve" written explicitly -- see elden-comments4.xml and elden-comments1-B19-excerpt.xml

legacyPlaceholder.doneStatusNeverAppearsInPlaceholderText: Confirmed: the B19 thread's root is done="1" (resolved) yet its legacy placeholder text (elden-comments1-B19-excerpt.xml) contains no resolved/closed marker of any kind -- just the literal comment/reply text.

tcAuthorLink.pattern: tc={GUID} where {GUID} is byte-identical (including case) to the corresponding threadedComment ROOT's id attribute
tcAuthorLink.alsoMirroredInXrUid: The legacy <comment> element's xr:uid attribute (xmlns:xr="http://schemas.microsoft.com/office/spreadsheetml/2014/revision") is ALSO set to that same root id -- confirmed in every sample.
tcAuthorLink.onlyLinkMechanism: Confirmed by spec text (MS-XLSX 'Legacy Comment Placeholders' page) and by every real sample: the tc={GUID} author string is the ONLY link between a legacy placeholder and its real thread. There is no relationship-level or ref-level link beyond this string convention plus the advisory 'ref should correspond' rule (spec: if refs mismatch, the legacy placeholder's own ref wins for display).

vmlComparison.objectTypeIdentical: Both legacy Notes (see ../xlsx-note-reference/vmlDrawing1.vml) and threaded-comment legacy placeholders use the exact same <x:ClientData ObjectType="Note"> shape -- there is no distinct ObjectType or VML marker for a threaded-comment placeholder.
vmlComparison.structuralDifferenceFound: ../xlsx-note-reference/vmlDrawing1.vml (a genuine legacy Note, Windows Excel) includes <x:Locked>True</x:Locked> and <x:LockText>True</x:LockText> inside ClientData. ALL THREE real threaded-comment-placeholder VML samples inspected (docling-vmlDrawing1.vml [Mac Excel], elden-vmlDrawing4.vml [Google Sheets], plus a third Windows-Excel sample inspected but not redistributed here -- see README) OMIT both <x:Locked> and <x:LockText> entirely. This 3-for-3 agreement across Mac Excel, Google Sheets and Windows Excel makes it a well-corroborated difference rather than a single-sample fluke.
vmlComparison.cosmeticOnlyDifferences: Self-closing vs. paired-empty tags (<x:MoveWithCells/> vs <x:MoveWithCells></x:MoveWithCells>), fillcolor as a literal hex (#ffffe1) vs a theme token (infoBackground [80]), and attribute/whitespace formatting are writer-specific styling, not meaningful to the format.

mixedNotesAndThreadedComments.sameWorkbookDifferentCells: Confirmed possible and unremarkable: docling-comments1.xml has genuine legacy Notes on A1/B2 (plain author names, no tc=) alongside threaded-comment placeholders on F7/G12 (tc=... authors) in the very same file/workbook.
mixedNotesAndThreadedComments.sameCellBothTypes: NOT independently verified either way by file inspection -- no sample encountered has both a real Note and a threaded comment on the identical cell. See README/report for the (unverified-by-us) community claim that Excel refuses this.

sourceFixtures.demonstrates: 2 threaded-comment threads (F7: root+1 reply, unresolved; G12: root only, unresolved) coexisting with 2 genuine legacy Notes (A1, B2) in one workbook.

sourceFixtures.authoringApp: Google Sheets xlsx export (no docProps/app.xml part at all; every person carries providerId="google-sheets")
sourceFixtures.demonstrates: done="1" resolved threads, done="0" explicit-unresolved threads, multi-reply flattening, and MULTIPLE independent threads sharing one cell ref (B19, 5 roots). Also contains a proprietary xl/documenttasks/documenttaskN.xml part (relationship type .../2019/04/relationships/documenttask) alongside the comments -- out of scope for this research but present and worth knowing about.
